描述_ZN: Scroll of The Emperor Daoguang Performing his Pleasure, Daoguang, Qing dynasty, on paper, color on paper, 111 cm in length and 294.5 cm in width.　　Emperor Daoguang of the Qing Dynasty showed his boldness when it came to matters as early as when he was an imperial son. Back then, Lin Qing of the Tianli Sect led an insurgent army to invade the Forbidden City when the Jiaqing Emperor was not in the palace (at the summer residence). When the palace was in a state of panic, Minning, who was 16 years old at the time, took the lead, raised his gun and shot at the rebels, and organized an effective resistance. He always kept the uprising army on the Qianqingmen Square outside the Qianqing Gate until the elite soldiers of the Eight Banners Jianrui Battalion arrived at the Forbidden City to relieve the siege. Minning's outstanding performance won him important leverage for his succession to the throne.　　The Daoguang emperor was at a critical moment in the turning point of history, but he "kept his usual but did not know his changes". During his 30-year reign, he abided by the ancestral system, was diligent in government, and was frugal. But the opium flowing from the southeast sea made him restless, and he finally resolved to strictly prohibit smoking. At the beginning of the 19th year of Daoguang (1839), the Daoguang Emperor appointed Lin Zexu as the Minister of the Imperial Household to combat smoking in Guangdong. The Tiger Gate Smoking Ban also caused tensions between China and Britain. In June 1840, the British expeditionary force reached the Chinese sea and the Opium War broke out. On August 29, 1842, the Qing government signed the Treaty of Nanjing, the first unequal treaty in modern Chinese history, with Britain, reducing China to a semi-colonial society. 　　This painting bears the seals of "Shen De Tang Bao", "Daoguang" and "Ri Jin Wu Jie".　　This picture was painted by a court painter and represents the court painting style of the late Qing Dynasty. It depicts the Emperor Daoguang and his princes and princesses having fun together in the Yuanmingyuan. In the painting, Emperor Daoguang is elegant, holding a snuff bottle, sitting in the pavilion of "Chengxin Zhengxue", looking kindly at his children playing. The fourth son of the emperor, Yi wisdom, who later became the Xianfeng emperor, and the sixth son of the emperor, Yi appeals, who later became the Prince Gong, were studying under the watchful eye of their father. The seventh son of the emperor, Yixuan, the eighth son of the emperor, and the ninth son of the emperor, Yixuan, are still young, and the seventh son of the emperor, Yixuan, is the grandfather of the later Xuantuan emperor, Puyi. The two princesses in the painting are Princess Shouan Gulun, the fourth daughter of the Daoguang Emperor, and Princess Shouen Gulun, the sixth daughter of the Daoguang Emperor.　　This picture has important historical value for studying the life of the late Qing Dynasty court.
